title: Handoff Weave: SDK Adaptors and Structured Tool Profiles (PRD draft)
content:
Summary:

This PRD describes a new surface we call the 'Handoff Weave': a minimal runtime contract and SDK adaptor pattern that makes progressive streaming + tool-calling + structured output ergonomics predictable for application developers across variable networks and client capabilities. The Weave focuses on three scenarios: low-latency mobile consumption, deterministic server-side replays for tool safety, and incremental structured commits for large responses.

Problem statement:
- Developers need streaming responses that can (a) quickly display partial results, (b) safely invoke downstream tools, and (c) commit structured fragments (JSON/records) as they arrive. Current hosted-api streaming semantics conflate textual deltas and tool events, making client SDKs implement brittle heuristics for ordering, idempotency, and resume.
- Mobile and edge clients have intermittent connectivity and memory constraints; naive full-session buffering or large JSON assembly causes latency or OOM.
- Observability and debugging across tool calls is limited when partial outputs are not uniquely addressable or replayable.

Goals:
1) Define a compact on-wire frame model (Weave frames) that separates presentation deltas, tool call events, and structured-commit fragments.
2) Provide SDK adaptors (JS/Swift/Go) implementing incremental commit APIs and a small resume/repair protocol so clients can recover mid-stream with minimal server coordination.
3) Ensure tool-calling safety: every tool call is annotated with an idempotency token, a causal anchor, and an optional quality-estimate field to enable safe automatic fallback to simpler models.
4) Improve observability: add per-frame telemetry hooks and a session ledger that surfaces replays, tool outcomes, and structured commit diffs in the Console.
5) Keep the Weave backward-compatible with existing streaming endpoints; fallback to legacy delta streams when clients don't understand typed frames.

Non-goals:
- Not addressing model-side hallucination detection or evaluation logic beyond surface telemetry fields.
- Not proposing an exhaustive typed-schema language for all possible structured outputs. We support pluggable small schemas (JSON Schemas) as an opt-in.

Design overview:
- Frame types:
  - PRES: presentation delta (for freeform text or UI-friendly snippets).
  - TOOL_REQ: tool call request envelope (includes tool_id, args, idempotency_token, anchor_frame_id).
  - TOOL_RES: tool response envelope (includes tool_id, success/failure, result_reference).
  - COMMIT: structured fragment to be persisted (includes schema_id, fragment_id, parent_fragment_id, patch_base_id, payload as JSON Patch or full object).
  - META: session-level signals (rollout hints, latency-budget updates, diagnostic breadcrumbs).

- Frame envelope fields (compact JSON line format over streaming):
  - frame_id (UUID), type (one of above), ts (ISO8601), anchor (optional frame_id), body (opaque string or JSON depending on type), sig (optional HMAC tag for enterprise).

Client SDK ergonomics (how clients use Weave):
- API surface (high-level):
  - createSession(opts): returns Session object with streaming socket or long-poll fallback.
  - session.on('presentation', fn(chunk, meta))
  - session.on('toolRequest', fn(toolReq)) -> returns a toolResponsePromise OR session.acceptToolCall(toolReq) to route to host tool adapters.
  - session.commit(schemaId, fragment): performs a COMMIT frame; returns commitAck with fragment_id and patch_base_id.
  - session.resumeFrom(frame_id): requests server to replay from anchor with minimal re-emit of dependent frames.

- Memory and bandwidth considerations: SDKs will offer a 'compact mode' that:
  - uses small frame_ids (base62) instead of UUID to save bytes,
  - switches COMMIT bodies to JSON Patch when fragment size > 2KB,
  - compresses consecutive PRES frames into a single PRES with delta-encoding.

Tool calling safety profile:
- Every TOOL_REQ must include: caller_session_id, idempotency_token, anchor_frame_id, input_hash, and optional quality_estimate.
- The server will accept TOOL_REQs if tool capacity is available for the declared tier; otherwise it emits a TOOL_RES with 'deferred' and suggests a fallback model (model_hint).
- Tools executed in Dedicated or Private deployments may carry an audit_handle (opaque string) to correlate with customer logs.

Structured commit model and conflict resolution:
- Each COMMIT is a first-class fragment with fragment_id and patch_base_id. The server maintains a lightweight CRDT-inspired patch ledger per session to merge non-conflicting commits; conflicting commits produce a MERGE_REQUIRED META frame.
- For typical usage (append-only transcripts, search documents, metadata stores) we expect clients to rely on last-writer-wins or explicit client-merge flows.

Observability and Console integration:
- Emit per-frame telemetry: frame_size_bytes, client_rtt_ms (when available), processing_latency_ms, tool_exec_latency_ms, tool_outcome (success|retryable_error|terminal_error), commit_merge_status.
- Expose a session ledger view: list of frames with visual diff for COMMIT fragments, tool call timelines, and replay controls (replay from frame X).
- Allow retention settings per-session for debug: ephemeral (7 days), standard (30 days), extended (90 days) for enterprise audit.

API examples (pseudo):
- Streaming example (client -> server):
  PRES frame: {"frame_id":"f1","type":"PRES","ts":"2024-10-20T14:22:10Z","body":"Analyzing repo..."}
  TOOL_REQ frame: {"frame_id":"f2","type":"TOOL_REQ","ts":"...","anchor":"f1","body":{"tool_id":"code-search:v2","args":{"query":"regex"},"idempotency":"tkn-123"}}
- Server responds: TOOL_RES with result_reference pointing to a COMMIT or a public artifact URL.

SDK migration plan and rollout:
- Phase 1 (alpha): JS SDK adaptor implements Weave in 'opt-in' mode; server returns legacy frames when client omits Weave header. Collect stability telemetry.
- Phase 2 (beta): Add Swift and Go SDKs, enable compact-mode. Expose console ledger beta.
- Phase 3 (GA): Default streaming endpoints advertise Weave; provide automatic translation layer for older SDKs; document migration steps for partners.

Backwards compatibility and fallbacks:
- If client doesn't implement Weave, server will emit textual PRES frames that contain embedded markers for tool calls (legacy behavior).
- Translation shim: when server receives TOOL_REQ from legacy client, server synthesizes a frame_id and emits TOOL_REQ->TOOL_RES in-line. However translation loses structured commit diffs and partial resume anchors.

Security and privacy considerations:
- COMMIT bodies may contain PII. By default COMMITs are stored encrypted at rest and access-controlled. For Private deployments, customers can supply a KMS key.
- HMAC 'sig' on frames can be enabled for high-assurance customers to detect tampering in transit across intermediaries.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Do we require schema registration (schema_id visibility) before first COMMIT? or allow ad-hoc schemas? Recommendation: allow ad-hoc but flag non-registered schemas in telemetry.
- How aggressive should automatic translation be for legacy clients vs preserving precise semantics? Translation simplifies adoption but hides incorrect client assumptions.
- Extent of CRDT merging; full CRDT model increases server complexity. We propose a lightweight three-way patch merge for GA.

Telemetry and eval metrics (success criteria):
- 95th percentile additional bytes/frame compared to legacy deltas < 18% in compact mode.
- Resume-from-anchor success rate >= 99% on stable networks, >= 92% on mobile networks.
- Tool-call idempotency misfires (duplicate tool executions per session) < 0.2% after rollout.
- Developer satisfaction (survey) target NPS >= 40 among early adopters.

Implementation notes for backend engineers:
- Streaming API will add X-Weave-Version header and accept a small binary prefix for compact frame ids.
- Persistence: session_ledger table (append-only) with indexes on session_id and frame_id; store minimal frame metadata and optionally body in an object store to avoid row inflation.
- Migration: add translation layer in the gateway to convert legacy tool markers to Weave frames for internal processing only.

Operational runbook highlights:
- If a MERGE_REQUIRED META frame is emitted, surface a console alert and mark session as needing manual review if merge attempts fail 3 times.
- Degraded mode: if commit ledger DB is overloaded, switch to append-only COMMITs with no merges and emit META frame with status 'degraded_commit_mode'.

Appendices:
A) SDK API snippets (JS):
  const s = await Redwood.createSession({model: 'rwd-stream-1', useWeave: true});
  s.on('presentation', (chunk, meta) => ui.append(chunk));
  s.on('toolRequest', async (req) => {
    // host app may route to local tool or call session.acceptToolCall(req)
    const result = await runLocalTool(req.body.args);
    await s.commit('search-fragment-v1', {results:result.items});
    return {handled: true};
  });

B) Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Increased bandwidth for heavyweight COMMIT frames. Mitigation: encourage JSON Patch and compact frame ids, and offer server-side compression for enterprise.
- Risk: Client complexity. Mitigation: provide reference adaptors and high-level helper methods that hide frame bookkeeping.

C) Next steps and owners:
- Prototype JS SDK adaptor and gateway translation: owner Marcus Alvarado (Q4 spike).
- Backend ledger prototype and merge worker: owner Priya Nair.
- Console session ledger UI: owner Lucía Gómez.

If this approach looks sound we will spin up a short cross-functional alpha sprint (2 weeks) to validate frame sizes, resume reliability, and tool safety signals.

Notes to reviewers: please focus on the client API ergonomics (are the helper functions sufficient?) and the commit merge model (is lightweight three-way patch merging acceptable for GA?).
